evidence.description: The use of the '!' operator to force unwrap the 'day' component from the dateComponents call.

candidates.explanation: Force unwrapping can lead to runtime crashes if the expected value is nil.
candidates.title: Force Unwrapping

evidence.description: The 'state' property performs a sort operation every time it is accessed.

candidates.explanation: Performing a sort operation inside a computed property can lead to performance issues if the property is accessed frequently, as it is an O(n log n) operation.
candidates.title: Inefficient Property Access

evidence.description: The 'decoder' property creates a new JSONDecoder instance every time it is accessed.

candidates.explanation: Creating a new instance of JSONDecoder repeatedly is inefficient; it should be instantiated once and reused.
candidates.title: Redundant Object Creation

evidence.description: An empty 'catch' block ignores potential errors during the file write operation.

candidates.explanation: Swallowing errors without logging or handling them makes debugging difficult and can hide critical issues like disk space errors or permission problems.
candidates.title: Silent Error Handling

evidence.description: The 'items' property is modified on a background dispatch queue ('dispatch') but accessed/read in 'state' and 'needsUpdate' without synchronization.

candidates.explanation: While 'items' is updated on a private background queue, it is accessed by other properties and methods without thread-safe mechanisms, which can lead to data races.
candidates.title: Potential Data Race
